additional_concerns: The source assigns continuing ultimate responsibility but supplies no complete test of effective retention or discharge through supervision. Governance, practical authority and conduct are possible evidence, not source-established necessary or sufficient conditions. No actual provider facts are supplied.

Retained accountability, adequate supervisory conduct and satisfactory operational outcomes must remain distinct. An operational failure alone does not establish displaced accountability; retained accountability alone does not establish fulfillment of all substantive duties.
Section 6.11C concerns third-party valuation. Its care, diligence, monitoring and review standard cannot automatically become a general tokenisation-supervision test.
The separate proper-records and operational-compatibility duty in s2 remains operative but is not a test of retained accountability.

Paragraph 14 and footnote 5 should be read together: confirmation is not expressly request-conditioned; demonstration is expressly request-conditioned in the main text. Footnote 5 specifies minimum compliance and smart-contract assurance content without repeating the trigger. Its wording leaves interpretive questions about independent demonstration and the reach of the satisfaction and high-confidence standards.

Absent an SFC request, the main-text demonstration trigger and the request-triggered third-party audit and legal-opinion duties in s5 and s6 are not activated. That does not remove confirmation or continuing substantive responsibilities. Audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion are distinct requirements.

Footnote 5 references paragraphs 10–13, whose complete text is not supplied. Broader fulfillment analysis requires the remaining applicable provisions and any relevant footnotes, including footnote 2.
Outsourcing is not an exception relieving responsibility. The exception label in the claim paired at p5 must not be implemented as an exemption.
The candidate has no executable expressions. Retrieval success and the unsupported structural-tool result establish neither legal fulfillment nor executable fidelity.
